s482cafe7cc24b4: In the modern Kubernetes cluster, multiple types of resources (e.g. CPU, memory, GPU, etc.) are usually managed on a unified platform. However, patterns and needs for different types of resources tend to vary significantly, leading to different strategic demands for stacking and dispersing resources.
s39ed34153a65cf: GPU resources: In an AI model training or reference mission, in order to maximize the use of GPU and reduce fragmentation, users usually wish to prioritize GPU tasks to a node (i.e. “cackling” strategy) that has been allocated to GPU. This strategy avoids waste of resources due to too wide a distribution of the GPU.
s1457d120da1614: CPU and memory resources: In contrast, the demand for CPU and memory resources is more diverse. For some online services or batching tasks, users tend to spread tasks over multiple nodes (i.e. “dispersion” strategies) in order to avoid resource hotspot problems at individual nodes, thereby improving the stability and performance of overall clusters.
s90a37ade25c0a3: In addition, in mixed workload scenarios, the needs of different missions for resources can interact. For example:
s014bf53ffed9fb: In a cluster where both GPU training missions and common CPU intensive tasks are run, if the CPU-intensive task is scheduling to the GPU node and consumes significant CPU and memory resources, it may result in subsequent GPU missions not being launched due to insufficient resources of the CPU, which eventually end up in Pending.
sfce594f1b5290b: In a multi-tenant environment, some users may only apply for CPU and memory resources, while others need GPU resources. If scheduler fails to distinguish between these needs, it can lead to resource competition and unfair resource allocation.
